title: The Komlos conjecture on vector balancing
statement: Given n, let K(n) be the infimum over all reals such that for every set of n vectors u_1,...,u_n in R^n with ||u_i||_2 <= 1 there exist signs eps_i in {-1,+1} with ||eps_1 u_1 + ... + eps_n u_n||_infinity <= K(n). Prove that there is a universal constant K with K(n) <= K for all n.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the Komlos conjecture and on matrix discrepancy. Banaszczyk's O(sqrt(log n)) bound remains the best unconditional result, with algorithmic versions (Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett) matching it; a constant bound is not known. The Randomstrasse101 open-problem compilations mined by the earlier ledgers in this campaign list matrix discrepancy problems adjacent to this one. Kept open.

attempt.method: Test what the probabilistic (random signs) benchmark gives and how far it is from the conjecture, so that the gap being attacked is explicit.
attempt.result: Random signs give, for each coordinate j, a sum of independent terms with variance sum_i u_i(j)^2, and the constraint ||u_i||_2 <= 1 bounds the sum over j of that variance by n, not each coordinate individually. So the worst case for random signs is all the mass in one coordinate: variance n, giving max coordinate of order sqrt(n log n) - the trivial bound. This is worth recording because it shows the conjecture is not a concentration statement at all: any proof must be a genuine partial colouring / convex-geometric argument, and the probabilistic method is off by a factor of sqrt(n log n), not by a logarithm. Banaszczyk's sqrt(log n) already exploits the convex body, and the remaining gap is exactly one square root of a logarithm.
attempt.obstruction: Banaszczyk's theorem produces a signing into any convex body of Gaussian measure at least 1/2 after scaling by 5; the cube of side sqrt(log n) is the smallest such cube, and the Gaussian measure threshold is what forces the logarithm. Removing it requires a balancing result for a body of small Gaussian measure, which the transference argument cannot give.
attempt.key_identity: Under ||u_i||_2 <= 1 the total coordinate variance is at most n but may concentrate in one coordinate, so random signs give only sqrt(n log n); the conjecture is a convex-geometry statement, not a concentration statement.

title: The Recht-Re noncommutative arithmetic-geometric mean inequality
statement: For any collection of d x d positive semidefinite matrices A_1,...,A_n, is it true that the spectral norm of (1/n!) sum over permutations sigma of the product A_{sigma(1)} ... A_{sigma(n)} is at most the spectral norm of (1/n^n) sum over all n-tuples (k_1,...,k_n) of the product A_{k_1} ... A_{k_n}? The source attributes conjecture (a) to Recht and Re, and records that it had been proved for n = 3 by Zhang.
resolved_by: Zehua Lai and Lek-Heng Lim, 'Recht-Re Noncommutative Arithmetic-Geometric Mean Conjecture is False', arXiv:2006.01510, ICML 2020. Comparing the objects BY NAME: the source calls conjecture (a) the Recht-Re inequality, citing [RR12] = Recht and Re, 'Toward a noncommutative arithmetic-geometric mean inequality', and states it for d x d positive semidefinite matrices with the spectral norm; Lai and Lim's abstract says 'A groundbreaking result of Recht and Re reduces the problem to a noncommutative analogue of the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality where n positive numbers are replaced by n positive definite matrices... The conjectured Recht-Re inequality has so far only been established for n = 2 and a special case of n = 3. We will show that the Recht-Re conjecture is false for general n... which we show are false as soon as n = 5.' Same named conjecture, same objects (n positive semidefinite matrices, sampling with versus without replacement), and the source's own n = 3 status matches the paper's. Correctly excluded. Note: Lai and Lim disprove the inequality without exhibiting explicit matrices, via a noncommutative Positivstellensatz reduction to a semidefinite program, so the counterexample is a certificate rather than a construction.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 'Recht-Re noncommutative arithmetic-geometric mean conjecture false counterexample Lai Lim'. Returned the arXiv abstract page 2006.01510 and the PMLR proceedings version; abstract read in full (quoted above), full text not fetched.

title: The reverse noncommutative arithmetic-geometric mean inequality
statement: For any collection of d x d positive semidefinite matrices A_1,...,A_n, is the spectral norm of (1/n!) sum over permutations sigma of A_{sigma(1)} ... A_{sigma(n)} at least the spectral norm of (1/n^n) sum over all n-tuples of A_{k_1} ... A_{k_n}? The source attributes conjecture (b) to Duchi and records that it had been proved for n = 3.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 as for E0043. Lai and Lim's paper is titled and stated for the RECHT-RE conjecture, which the source identifies as direction (a) with citation [RR12]; direction (b) is attributed by the source to a different reference, [Duc12]. I found no paper resolving direction (b), and Lai-Lim's abstract does not name it. Comparing objects by name, the refutation covers (a) and not (b), so this row is kept ADMITTED. That distinction is exactly the kind of check the D-ledger's audit flagged as necessary.

attempt.method: Check whether the two directions can both be false, or whether one direction is forced, by testing the commuting case and a rank-one case.
attempt.result: When the A_i commute both sides are the same product of scalars in different orders and the two conjectures both hold with equality on the spectrum, so no commuting example distinguishes them - which is why the problem is genuinely noncommutative. For rank-one A_i = v_i v_i^T the products telescope: A_{k_1}...A_{k_n} = (prod of inner products) v_{k_1} v_{k_n}^T, so both averages become explicit sums over words weighted by chains of inner products, and direction (b) asserts that the permutation average of such chains dominates the free average. Since permutations force all n vectors to appear exactly once while the free average is dominated by the single repeated word with the largest self-overlap, direction (b) is FALSE on rank-one examples with one dominant vector: taking v_1 = e_1 and v_2,...,v_n tiny makes the free average of order ||v_1||^{2n} while every permutation product contains all the tiny vectors. This is a candidate refutation, stated as such - I have not verified the constants, and the correct comparison requires the two normalisations 1/n! and 1/n^n to be handled carefully, so it should be checked before being believed.
attempt.obstruction: The rank-one reduction makes both sides computable but the normalisations differ, and the tiny-vector construction may violate the implicit assumption that the A_i are comparable. A proper check needs the exact inequality with both normalisations at n = 4 or 5, which is a finite semidefinite feasibility problem of the same kind Lai and Lim solved for direction (a).
attempt.key_identity: For rank-one A_i = v_i v_i^T every ordered product collapses to a chain of inner products times v_first v_last^T, which makes both averages explicit and turns the conjecture into a comparison of two weighted word sums.

title: The optimal basis for the largest d-dimensional projection of a Gaussian vector
locator: Open Problem 1.1 (A. Mallat and Zeitouni), PDF p. 14
statement: Let g be N(0, Sigma) in R^p with Sigma known, and let d < p. For an orthonormal basis V = [v_1,...,v_p] let Gamma_V be the squared l_2 norm of the largest projection of g onto a subspace spanned by d elements of V, i.e. the max over subsets S of size d of the sum over i in S of (v_i^T g)^2. Which basis V maximises E[Gamma_V]? Mallat and Zeitouni conjecture the optimal basis is the eigenbasis of Sigma; this is known for d = 1 and open for d > 1.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the Mallat-Zeitouni conjecture on the best basis for the largest projection of a Gaussian vector. Found the original 2011 preprint and citations describing the conjecture as open; no resolution found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Isolate why d = 1 is easy and what breaks at d = 2, by writing the objective as an expected maximum over subsets.
attempt.result: For d = 1 the objective is E max_i (v_i^T g)^2, a maximum of p correlated squared Gaussians with variances v_i^T Sigma v_i summing to trace(Sigma). Since a maximum of Gaussians is maximised by making the variances as UNEQUAL as possible under a fixed sum, and the eigenbasis is the unique basis realising the extreme point of the majorisation order on the variance vector, the d = 1 case is a Schur-convexity statement. For d >= 2 the objective is the maximum over subsets of SUMS of d such squares, and the relevant vector of subset-variances is no longer the image of the basis under a fixed linear map: two different bases can give the same multiset of individual variances but different subset sums, because the correlations between the (v_i^T g)^2 differ. So the d = 1 proof does not degrade quantitatively at d = 2 - it fails structurally, because Schur convexity in the variance vector is no longer the right order. Naming the correct order (majorisation on the vector of subset variances, which is not determined by the individual variances) is the useful step.
attempt.obstruction: The eigenbasis makes the coordinates independent, which maximises the spread of the subset sums but minimises their positive correlation; for d >= 2 the expected maximum over subsets can be increased by correlation, and the two effects pull in opposite directions with no known comparison. A counterexample, if one exists, will be a basis mixing the top eigenvectors so that several subsets are simultaneously large.
attempt.key_identity: For d = 1 the objective depends on the basis only through the variance vector (v_i^T Sigma v_i), and the eigenbasis is its majorisation-extreme point; for d >= 2 it depends on the joint law of subset sums, which the variance vector does not determine.

title: Monotonicity in n of the expected average singular value of a Gaussian matrix
locator: Open Problem 1.2 (Monotonicity of singular values), PDF p. 17
statement: Let X be an n x n matrix with i.i.d. N(0,1) entries and let sigma_R(n) be the expected value of the average singular value of n^{-1/2} X, with sigma_C(n) the complex-Gaussian analogue. It is conjectured that sigma_C(n+1) <= sigma_C(n) for all n >= 1 (and the corresponding monotonicity in the real case).
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on monotonicity in the dimension of the expected average singular value of Ginibre matrices. Found the Bandeira-Kennedy-Singer source of the conjecture and later work on moments of the Marchenko-Pastur law; no proof of the monotonicity for all n was found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Compare with the limit, since the quantity converges and the conjecture is that the convergence is one-sided.
attempt.result: The average singular value of n^{-1/2} X converges to the first absolute moment of the quarter-circle law, which is 8/(3 pi) = 0.8488..., so monotone decreasing to that limit is the conjecture's content and any proof must therefore show the finite-n value EXCEEDS 8/(3 pi) for every n, which is already a nontrivial one-sided statement. The natural exact route is the known finite-n formula: for the complex Ginibre ensemble the squared singular values are the eigenvalues of a complex Wishart matrix with a Laguerre-ensemble joint density, and E[average singular value] is a single integral against the Laguerre kernel, hence a ratio of Gamma functions and a hypergeometric term. Monotonicity in n then becomes an inequality between two explicit hypergeometric expressions, which is a finite computation in principle. Recording this as the route is the useful output; I have not carried out the hypergeometric comparison.
attempt.obstruction: The Laguerre-kernel expression for E[sigma-bar] is not a ratio of Gamma functions alone - it involves a sum over the n Laguerre polynomials - so the n to n+1 comparison is not termwise, and the standard tool (interlacing of the singular values of X and of X with a row removed) compares the n x n and n x (n+1) ensembles, not the n x n and (n+1) x (n+1) ones with the differing n^{-1/2} normalisation.
attempt.key_identity: The average singular value of n^{-1/2} X converges to the first absolute moment of the quarter-circle law, 8/(3 pi); the conjecture asserts monotone decrease to that limit, so it entails the one-sided bound E[sigma-bar(n)] > 8/(3 pi) for every n.

title: Threshold for rank-constrained semidefinite relaxations of the spiked Wigner model
locator: Open Problem 1.3 (Spike model for rank constrained SDP), PDF p. 23
statement: Let W be a Wigner matrix with i.i.d. N(0,1) entries, and for symmetric B define Q_r(B) = max{trace(BX) : X psd, X_ii = 1, rank(X) <= r}, and q_r(lambda) = lim_{n to infinity} (1/n) E Q_r((lambda/n) 11^T + n^{-1/2} W). What is the value of lambda_r^* = inf{lambda >= 0 : ...}, the threshold above which the rank-r constrained relaxation detects the spike?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on rank-constrained SDP thresholds for the spiked Wigner model and on the Z2 synchronisation SDP. The r = 1 (integer) and r = infinity (full SDP) cases are understood via the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy and the Montanari-Sen analysis; the intermediate finite-r thresholds are governed by the vector spin glass free energy and I found no explicit determination. Kept open.

attempt.method: Identify q_r(lambda) with a known free energy, since the maximisation over rank-r psd matrices with unit diagonal is a spin system on the sphere.
attempt.result: Writing X = sigma sigma^T with sigma_i in S^{r-1} (unit vectors in R^r), the constraint set is exactly the configuration space of the r-component vector spin model, and (1/n) Q_r is the ground-state energy of the r-vector Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with an added ferromagnetic term of strength lambda. So q_r(lambda) is the zero-temperature limit of the vector-SK free energy with external ferromagnetic coupling, and lambda_r^* is the ferromagnetic-transition point of that model. This is not stated in the source and it converts the problem into one with an existing machinery: the Panisi-type variational formula for vector spin glasses (Panchenko) gives q_r(lambda) as a variational problem, and lambda_r^* is where the optimiser becomes non-trivial. The reduction is exact; the evaluation of the resulting variational problem at finite r is not carried out here.
attempt.obstruction: The vector-SK Parisi formula is a variational problem over monotone matrix paths rather than scalar paths, and its zero-temperature limit is not known in closed form for any r >= 2, so the reduction transfers the problem to another one that is open, albeit better studied. For r = 1 the answer follows from the Parisi formula for the SK model with ferromagnetic interaction; the source's question is exactly the r >= 2 case.
attempt.key_identity: Rank-r psd matrices with unit diagonal are exactly Gram matrices of unit vectors in R^r, so Q_r is the ground-state energy of the r-component vector spin glass with a ferromagnetic term, and lambda_r^* is its ferromagnetic transition.

title: Improving the noncommutative Khintchine inequality to a square-root logarithm
locator: Open Problem 4.1 and Conjecture 4.21, PDF p. 69
statement: Let A_1,...,A_n be symmetric d x d matrices and g_1,...,g_n i.i.d. N(0,1). Prove or disprove that E||sum_k g_k A_k|| <= sigma + C (log d)^{1/2} sigma_*, where sigma is the strong variance ||sum A_k^2||^{1/2} and sigma_* the weak variance. The source notes that the conjecture may be false but that no counterexample is known.
status_search: Checked the arXiv abstract of Bandeira, Boedihardjo and van Handel, 'Matrix Concentration Inequalities and Free Probability', arXiv:2108.06312 (Inventiones 2023), which develops nonasymptotic bounds capturing noncommutativity and 'intrinsic freeness'. Comparing objects by name: the conjecture asks for the prefactor (log d)^{1/2} on the weak variance sigma_*; the abstract claims bounds that are sharp where the noncommutative Khintchine inequality is suboptimal, and the bound in that line of work carries (log d)^{3/4} rather than (log d)^{1/2}. On that reading the conjectured exponent 1/2 is NOT established, so the row is kept ADMITTED. I read the abstract, not the paper; a merger should check the exact exponent in the published version before treating this as open.

attempt.method: Check the conjecture against the two extreme cases that any candidate bound must reproduce, to see whether the exponent 1/2 is even the right guess.
attempt.result: When the A_k commute and are diagonal, the norm is a maximum of d independent Gaussians with variances given by the rows, so E||X|| is of order sigma_* sqrt(log d) exactly, and sigma can be as small as sigma_*; the conjecture is TIGHT there, which is the source's reason for the exponent. At the opposite extreme, when the A_k are free-like (independent GUE-type), E||X|| tends to 2 sigma with no logarithm at all, so the conjecture is far from tight there but not violated. The conjecture therefore asserts that the commuting case is the worst, and that is a statement about interpolation between the two extremes. A caution about what a proof would NOT be: the trivial bound E||X|| <= sigma + sqrt(2 log d) times max_k ||A_k|| follows from a union bound over a net and is weaker than the conjecture whenever sigma_* is much smaller than max_k ||A_k||, so the conjecture is genuinely stronger than the union bound and any argument reproducing only the union bound is not progress.
attempt.obstruction: The two extremes are separated by the free-probability quantity that BBvH call intrinsic freeness, and the known interpolation loses a factor because the noncommutative moment method must control all moments simultaneously; the (log d)^{3/4} exponent in the literature comes from optimising a trace-moment bound of order p, and the gap to 1/2 is exactly the gap between a moment bound and a supremum bound over a net.
attempt.key_identity: For commuting diagonal A_k the norm is a maximum of d Gaussians and the (log d)^{1/2} is attained; for free-like A_k the norm is 2 sigma with no logarithm, so the conjecture asserts that the commuting case is extremal.

title: The Latala-Riemer-Schutt comparison for Gaussian random matrices
statement: Given X a symmetric random matrix with independent Gaussian entries, is E||X|| comparable to E max_k ||X e_k||_2? The source notes that Bandeira-van Handel answer this positively for a large range of variance profiles but not in full generality, and that van Handel had proved it in a special case.
resolved_by: Rafal Latala, Ramon van Handel and Pierre Youssef, 'The dimension-free structure of nonhomogeneous random matrices', Inventiones mathematicae 214 (2018); arXiv:1711.00807. Comparing the objects BY NAME: the source's question names 'X a symmetric random matrix with independent gaussian entries' and asks whether E||X|| is comparable to E max_k ||X e_k||_2. The paper's abstract, read in full via the arXiv API, opens 'Let X be a symmetric random matrix with independent but non-identically distributed centered Gaussian entries. We show that E||X||_{S_p} is comparable (with universal constants) to E[(sum_i (sum_j X_ij^2)^{p/2})^{1/p}] for any 2 <= p <= infinity', and adds 'This settles, in the case p = infinity, a conjecture of the first author'. At p = infinity the left side is E||X|| (the spectral norm is the S_infinity norm) and the right side is E[max_i (sum_j X_ij^2)^{1/2}] = E max_i ||X e_i||_2 for symmetric X. Same hypothesis, same two quantities, universal constants - this is exactly the source's question. Correctly excluded.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for the Latala-Riemer-Schutt conjecture, then the arXiv API abstract of 1711.00807 read verbatim (quoted above). Full text not fetched; the identification rests on the abstract's own statement of hypothesis and conclusion, which match the source's question term by term.

title: The matrix Spencer conjecture
locator: Open Problem 4.3 and Conjecture 4.23 (Matrix Six-Deviations Suffice), PDF p. 70
statement: Is there a universal constant C such that for any n symmetric matrices H_1,...,H_n in R^{n x n} with ||H_k|| <= 1 there exist signs eps_1,...,eps_n in {-1,+1} with ||sum_k eps_k H_k|| <= C sqrt(n)? When the H_k are diagonal this is Spencer's six standard deviations theorem.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 'matrix Spencer conjecture six deviations status resolved 2024'. Bansal, Jiang and Meka, 'Resolving matrix Spencer conjecture up to poly-logarithmic rank' (STOC 2023, arXiv:2208.11286) prove it for matrices of rank at most n/log^3 n. The search also returned a 2026 arXiv item titled 'A Proof of the Matrix Spencer Conjecture' (arXiv 2608.28816) which I did NOT read and which is an unrefereed preprint. Per the campaign's rule of admitting rather than excluding when in doubt, this row is kept ADMITTED with that preprint recorded as the lead that must be checked before anyone treats the problem as closed.

attempt.method: Calibrate against the random signing and against the diagonal case, to see where the sqrt(n) must come from.
attempt.result: Random signs give, by the matrix Chernoff/Khintchine bound, ||sum eps_k H_k|| of order sigma sqrt(log n) with sigma = ||sum H_k^2||^{1/2} <= sqrt(n), i.e. sqrt(n log n) - so exactly as in the scalar Spencer theorem, the random signing is off by sqrt(log n) and the conjecture asks for the partial-colouring gain. The rank restriction in the known result is not incidental: for rank-r matrices the effective dimension in the matrix Khintchine bound is n r rather than n^2, so the logarithm becomes log(nr) and the partial-colouring argument has room. The conjecture in full rank is therefore exactly the statement that the matrix Khintchine logarithm can be removed in the same way Spencer removed the scalar one - and by E0048 the logarithm in matrix Khintchine is itself not known to be improvable, so the two problems are linked: an affirmative answer to Open Problem 4.1 with the (log d)^{1/2} exponent would not by itself give matrix Spencer, but a bound with no logarithm at all would.
attempt.obstruction: Spencer's partial colouring lemma works in the cube with a body defined by n linear constraints; the matrix version needs a body defined by a spectral constraint, whose Gaussian measure is controlled only through the same matrix concentration inequality that carries the logarithm. The argument is therefore circular unless one has a logarithm-free spectral bound for a restricted class, which is what the rank restriction supplies.
attempt.key_identity: Random signs give sqrt(n log n) by matrix Khintchine, and the rank-r restriction replaces the dimension n^2 by n r in that bound, which is exactly the room the known partial result uses.

title: Concentration of the spectral norm of random k-lifts of graphs
locator: Open Problem 4.5 (Random k-lifts of graphs), PDF p. 78
statement: Give a tight upper bound for E||A_{pi^k} - E A_{pi^k}||, where A_{pi^k} is the adjacency matrix of a random k-lift of a graph on n vertices. The source records Oliveira's bound of essentially sqrt(log(nk)) and notes that results of Amit-Bhatia-Grimmett-type suggest more concentration for large k, and that k = 2 reduces to a matrix Bernstein estimate.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 'Bordenave Collins eigenvalues of random lifts strong asymptotic freeness'. Charles Bordenave and Benoit Collins, 'Eigenvalues of random lifts and polynomials of random permutation matrices', Annals of Mathematics 190 (2019) 811-875 (arXiv:1801.00876) show that the nontrivial eigenvalues of random n-lifts of a FIXED base graph approximately achieve the Alon-Boppana bound with high probability as the lift degree tends to infinity. Comparing objects by name: the source asks for a bound on E||A - EA|| for a k-lift of a graph on n vertices, wanting the dependence on BOTH n and k; Bordenave-Collins fix the base graph (hence n) and let the lift degree grow. Different quantifiers, so the row is kept ADMITTED, with Bordenave-Collins recorded as resolving the large-k fixed-n regime and as the obvious first thing to try to make uniform.

attempt.method: Write down what each of the two known regimes gives and where they must meet.
attempt.result: Oliveira's matrix-Bernstein bound gives sqrt(log(nk)) because the ambient dimension of the lift is nk; Bordenave-Collins give the dimension-free constant 2 sqrt(d-1) for fixed n and k tending to infinity. These two are compatible only if the logarithm in Oliveira's bound is an artefact of the dimension counting, and the natural conjecture the two regimes force is a bound of the form C sqrt(d) + o(1) uniformly in k, with the logarithm appearing only through n. That is: the correct conjecture is not 'more concentration for large k' but 'no k-dependence at all beyond the base graph's spectral data'. Stating the conjecture in that form, forced by matching the two regimes, is the useful output; no proof of uniformity is offered.
attempt.obstruction: The trace method that gives Bordenave-Collins their result counts non-backtracking walks in the lift and is asymptotic in k with the base graph fixed; making it uniform in n requires controlling the number of walks in a growing base graph, where the combinatorial estimates degrade. Conversely matrix Bernstein cannot see the non-backtracking structure at all, which is where the logarithm is lost.
attempt.key_identity: A k-lift of an n-vertex graph is an nk-dimensional object, so matrix Bernstein pays sqrt(log(nk)); the non-backtracking trace method pays nothing in k, so the two regimes together force a conjecture with no k-dependence.

title: A sharp lower bound on the probability that a sum of nonnegative unit-mean variables exceeds its mean plus one
locator: Open Problem 4.6 and Conjecture 4.33, PDF p. 78
statement: Let X_1,...,X_n be independent random variables with X_i >= 0 and E X_i = 1 for every i. Prove or disprove that P(sum_i X_i <= n + 1) >= 1 - 1/e. The source notes that the bound is attained in the limit by the i.i.d. example X_i = n+1 with probability 1/(n+1) and 0 otherwise, for which the probability is 1 - (n/(n+1))^n, decreasing to 1 - 1/e.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on Feige's inequality and the 1 - 1/e conjecture for nonnegative independent variables with unit mean. Feige's original result gives a constant of 1/13, improved to 0.1798 (He, Zhang and Zhang) and further by later work; the sharp constant 1 - 1/e remains conjectural as far as the search showed. Kept open.

attempt.method: Check the conjecture against the extremal example and against the trivial bound, since the campaign's own audit found a case where a 'result' turned out to be Markov's inequality in disguise.
attempt.result: Markov gives P(sum > n+1) <= n/(n+1), i.e. P(sum <= n+1) >= 1/(n+1), which tends to 0 and is vastly weaker than 1 - 1/e - so the conjecture is genuinely more than the trivial bound, unlike the case the D-ledger audit caught. The extremal example is the two-point law at 0 and n+1, and it is worth noting that it is extremal in a strong sense: it puts the whole deviation into a single atom just above the threshold, so any proof must handle laws with an atom at exactly n+1 and cannot use any smoothness. A useful consequence of the extremal example: the conjecture cannot be improved to any constant larger than 1 - 1/e, and it is attained only in the limit, so the inequality should be strict for every finite n. That strictness is a checkable weaker statement.
attempt.obstruction: The difficulty is that the X_i need share no scale: some may be bounded and others heavy-tailed with the same mean, so no single truncation works, and the standard reduction to two-point laws (which is available for many such extremal problems by a Choquet argument) is blocked because the constraint set - independent, nonnegative, unit mean - is not compact in a topology making the objective continuous.
attempt.key_identity: Markov gives only P(sum <= n+1) >= 1/(n+1), so the conjectured 1 - 1/e is not a restatement of the trivial bound; the extremal two-point law at 0 and n+1 attains 1 - (n/(n+1))^n, which decreases to 1 - 1/e.

title: Sum of maximum and minimum bisection of a random regular graph
locator: Open Problem 8.5 and Conjecture 8.5, PDF p. 117
statement: Let G be a uniformly random d-regular graph on n vertices. Prove or disprove that for every d, as n grows, (1/n)(MaxBis(G) + MinBis(G)) = d/2 + o(1), where MaxBis and MinBis are the maximum and minimum bisection sizes. The source notes that the conjecture is known to hold up to o(sqrt(d)) terms by Dembo-Montanari-Sen.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on maximum and minimum bisection of random regular graphs and the Zdeborova-Boettcher conjecture. Dembo, Montanari and Sen (arXiv:1503.03923) establish the extremal cut values up to o(sqrt(d)) via the Parisi formula, and later work (Sen; Jagannath-Sen) refines the constants; I found no proof for fixed small d. Kept open.

attempt.method: Test the conjecture against the two regimes it must reconcile: large d, where the Parisi machinery applies, and small d, where it does not.
attempt.result: For large d the interpolation gives MaxBis/n = d/4 + P_* sqrt(d)/2 + o(sqrt(d)) and MinBis/n = d/4 - P_* sqrt(d)/2 + o(sqrt(d)) with P_* the Parisi constant, so the SUM is d/2 + o(sqrt(d)) automatically - the conjecture at large d is the statement that the two sqrt(d) corrections cancel EXACTLY, which the interpolation gives only to within o(sqrt(d)). So the conjecture's content at large d is an exact symmetry between the max and min problems, not a computation of either. At small d the interpolation is unavailable and the conjecture is a statement about the local structure of the random regular graph; the source itself points to Lyons's bounds as meaningful already at d = 3. Separating 'the corrections cancel' from 'the corrections are known' is the useful step: the conjecture is a symmetry claim.
attempt.obstruction: The exact cancellation would follow from a sign symmetry exchanging the max-cut and min-cut problems, and no such symmetry exists on a fixed graph - it holds only in distribution and only to leading order, because the random regular graph is not bipartite and MinBis is bounded below by an odd-girth obstruction that has no MaxBis counterpart. Quantifying that asymmetry at fixed d is exactly the missing piece.
attempt.key_identity: Both extremal bisections equal d/4 plus or minus the same Parisi correction to leading order, so the conjecture is that the two sqrt(d) corrections cancel exactly, a symmetry statement rather than an evaluation.

title: Partial recovery threshold for the balanced stochastic block model with more than three communities
statement: For the balanced stochastic block model with k > 3 constant communities, inner connection probability a/n and outer probability b/n, what is the threshold at which it becomes possible to produce an estimate correlating with the true partition (the partial recovery, or detection, threshold)?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the detection threshold for the stochastic block model with more than three communities. Abbe and Sandon showed that for k >= 4 the Kesten-Stigum bound is NOT the detection threshold in the disassortative case, and gave algorithms below it; Banks-Moore-Neeman-Netrapalli give information-theoretic bounds showing a gap for large k. The exact threshold for k >= 4 remains unknown as far as the search showed. Kept open.

attempt.method: State the two bounds that bracket the answer, and check whether the gap is an artefact or intrinsic.
attempt.result: The Kesten-Stigum bound (a-b)^2 = k(a + (k-1)b) is the reconstruction threshold for the broadcast process on the Galton-Watson tree that describes the local limit, and it is exactly the point where the second eigenvalue of the broadcast kernel crosses the branching-number threshold. For k <= 3 tree reconstruction and Kesten-Stigum coincide; for k >= 4 they do not, and the local-limit correspondence shows the SBM detection threshold equals the TREE RECONSTRUCTION threshold, not Kesten-Stigum. So the question is not open as a graph question at all - it is exactly the open problem of determining the reconstruction threshold for the k-state symmetric channel on a Poisson tree, which is a cleaner and older problem. Saying that is the useful reduction: the source poses it as an SBM question and the mathematical content is entirely in the tree.
attempt.obstruction: The tree reconstruction threshold for the symmetric k-state channel is known only through bounds (Mossel-Peres for the non-reconstruction side, Sly for k = 3, and asymptotics in k); an exact value for any k >= 4 is not known, and the non-reconstruction side requires a contraction estimate for the belief-propagation recursion that fails to be a simple second-moment computation once the Kesten-Stigum bound is not tight.
attempt.key_identity: The local weak limit of the sparse SBM is a Galton-Watson tree with a k-state symmetric broadcast, so the detection threshold IS the tree reconstruction threshold; Kesten-Stigum is the second-eigenvalue bound and is strictly loose for k >= 4.

title: Convergence threshold for the projected power method in the spiked Wigner model
statement: In the synchronisation model Y = z z^T + sigma W with z in {-1,+1}^n and W a Wigner matrix, for which values of sigma does the projected power method converge to the optimal solution of the maximum-likelihood problem, or at least to a solution correlating well with z, with high probability?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the projected power method for Z2 synchronisation and its convergence threshold. Later work (Chen-Candes on projected power methods, and the AMP literature of Deshpande-Abbe-Montanari) gives sharp thresholds for approximate message passing in this model; whether those thresholds transfer to the projected power method with a random or spectral initialisation was not established by the search. Kept open with the AMP results recorded as the natural comparison.

attempt.method: Separate the question into the two things a power-method analysis needs: a basin of attraction and an initialisation inside it.
attempt.result: With spectral initialisation the analysis is essentially settled by the BBP transition: the top eigenvector of Y correlates with z as soon as sigma < sqrt(n), and one step of the projected power method improves the correlation monotonically, so the interesting regime is sigma of order sqrt(n) and the question is about constants, not orders. With RANDOM initialisation the picture is different: the iteration is then a nonconvex landscape question and the relevant threshold is where spurious local maxima of the likelihood disappear. So the source's single question is two questions with different answers, and the informative one is the random-initialisation case. That separation, and the observation that the spectral case reduces to BBP, is the useful step.
attempt.obstruction: For random initialisation the first iterate is nearly orthogonal to z, so the signal appears only at second order and the analysis requires controlling the whole trajectory of a nonconvex iteration, for which the only available tool is a state-evolution argument that is proved for approximate message passing (with its Onsager correction) and not for the plain projected power method, whose iterates are correlated with the noise.
attempt.key_identity: With spectral initialisation the threshold is the BBP transition at sigma of order sqrt(n) and the projected power iteration only improves correlation; the genuinely open case is random initialisation, where the signal enters only at second order.

title: Tightness of the semidefinite relaxation for Z2 synchronisation up to the optimal noise level
statement: Prove or disprove: with high probability the semidefinite relaxation of the Z2 synchronisation maximum-likelihood problem is tight as long as sigma = O(n^{1/2}) up to logarithmic factors. The source notes this would follow from showing that ||W x^*||_infinity = O(n^{1/2}) up to logarithms, where x^* is the optimal solution.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on tightness of the SDP relaxation for Z2 synchronisation. Bandeira-Boumal-Voroninski and Abbe-Bandeira-Hall give tightness in the regime sigma = O(n^{1/4}) and its refinements; later work pushed the exponent, and I did not establish whether n^{1/2} up to logarithms has been reached. Kept admitted with that uncertainty recorded.

attempt.method: Examine the sufficient condition the source names and test whether it can hold, since it involves the optimal solution rather than a fixed vector.
attempt.result: For a FIXED vector x independent of W, ||W x||_infinity is of order sqrt(n log n) by a union bound over n coordinates, so the sufficient condition is exactly what one would get if x^* were independent of the noise. The whole difficulty, and the reason the condition is not immediate, is that x^* is a function of W: it is the maximiser of x^T W x over the cube, so it is aligned with the noise, and the naive union bound does not apply. This is the same measurability obstruction as in E0033 (first-passage percolation geodesics). Quantifying it: the maximiser over 2^n sign vectors makes the effective union bound over 2^n vectors rather than n, which would give ||W x||_infinity of order n, not sqrt(n log n) - so a proof must exploit that x^* is close to z and hence nearly independent of W, and the residual dependence is what must be controlled.
attempt.obstruction: Controlling the residual dependence requires a leave-one-out argument in which one coordinate of the noise is resampled and the maximiser is shown to move little - which is exactly the kind of stability that fails near the threshold, where the likelihood landscape has near-ties.
attempt.key_identity: For x independent of W a union bound gives ||W x||_infinity of order sqrt(n log n), but the optimiser x^* is selected using W, and a union bound over all 2^n sign vectors would give only order n - the gap is the residual dependence of x^* on the noise.

title: Consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator for multireference alignment
statement: (1) Is the quasi-maximum-likelihood (or the maximum-likelihood) estimator consistent for the multireference alignment problem, after fixing the power spectrum appropriately? (2) For a given signal length L and noise level sigma, how large must the number of observations n be to allow reasonably accurate recovery in the multireference alignment problem?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the sample complexity of multireference alignment. Part (2) is answered by Perry, Weed, Bandeira, Rigollet and Singer, 'The sample complexity of multireference alignment' (SIAM J. Math. Data Sci. 2019), which establishes that n of order sigma^6 samples are necessary and sufficient in the generic case (and sigma^4 with known distribution of shifts) - this is a resolution of the source's part (2) and is recorded here rather than used to drop the row, because part (1), the consistency of the (quasi-)MLE, is a different statement about a different object (the estimator, not the sample complexity) and I found no resolution of it. Row kept ADMITTED for part (1).

attempt.method: Ask what the sample-complexity answer implies about the estimator question, since the two are related but not equivalent.
attempt.result: The sigma^6 rate comes from the third moment: the first two moments of the observations are invariant under the group action in a way that loses the phases, and the bispectrum (the third moment) is the first invariant that determines the signal, with estimation error of order sigma^3 / sqrt(n). Consistency of the MLE is a different claim: it asserts that maximising the likelihood, not the method of invariant moments, recovers the signal. The two agree only if the likelihood's population maximiser is unique up to the group, and the moment analysis shows precisely that the population second moment does NOT identify the signal - so the MLE's identifiability rests on the third-order behaviour of the likelihood at the true parameter, where the Fisher information degenerates. That degeneracy is the reason the question is nontrivial and the reason the sigma^6 rate is not sigma^2.
attempt.obstruction: With a degenerate Fisher information the standard consistency proof (uniform law of large numbers plus a well-separated maximum) fails at the rate that matters: the likelihood surface is flat to second order along the directions the group action mixes, and controlling the empirical process on a flat surface requires uniform control at scale sigma^3, which is exactly the sample-complexity computation and not a corollary of it.
attempt.key_identity: The first two moments of multireference alignment observations do not identify the signal and the third (the bispectrum) does, which is why the sample complexity is of order sigma^6; the same degeneracy makes the Fisher information vanish and blocks the standard MLE consistency argument.
